items.title: AppleCare+ Launched 15 Years Ago Today
items.snippet: AppleCare+ became available for the first time 15 years ago today, on October 14, 2011, alongside the iPhone 4S, following its announcement ten days earlier. The previous $69 AppleCare Protection Plan in the United States extended hardware repair coverage and technical support to two years, but excluded accidental damage. ‌AppleCare‌+ cost $99, retaining that two-year term while adding coverage for two accidental damage incidents, each with a $49 service fee. So in 2027, it will turn 20 years old, and rumors point to Apple commemorating the event with a special 20th-anniversary model. items.title: Hyper-V enhanced session mode: VMConnect no longer redirects smart cards, WebAuthn, and printers by default
items.snippet: The October 13, 2026 security update changes how Hyper-V Virtual Machine Connection ( VMConnect ) handles device redirection in enhanced session mode. By default, printers, smart cards, and WebAuthn credentials—including Windows Hello and FIDO2 security keys—are no longer passed through to a virtual machine (VM) unless you turn those options on. Clipboard sharing and audio playback still default to enabled. Sensitive redirections now appear on the first page of the connection dialog, and you get one prompt per VM to confirm your choices. items.title: AI Illiteracy: Only 0.24% truly understand AI's capabilities
items.snippet: AI pioneer Andrej Karpathy is an Anthropic AI researcher and educator who co-founded OpenAI and later served as Tesla’s director of AI. His rough estimate puts just 0.24% of people among those who understand AI’s potential and know how to use it: billions have little or no experience with language models, while about 20 million professionals use frontier systems and roughly 5,000 have access inside AI labs. Most users still treat AI as a chatbot or a better search engine rather than a means of orchestrating agent swarms for complex tasks, a skill that is much harder to acquire than expected. Source
